title: A Multimodal Generative AI Framework for Predicting the Toxicity of Nanoparticles
summary: Assembles a nanoparticle toxicity table by pulling heterogeneous values out of the literature with an LLM and encoding the free-text toxicity summaries as SciBERT embeddings, then generates candidate nanoparticles with a target toxicity index and checks the winner against coarse-grained molecular dynamics in GROMACS. Four generators — CTGAN, TVAE, WGAN-GP and TabDDPM — compete on the assembled table. SDV supplies two of the four and, more decisively, the quality score that ranks all four: TabDDPM is selected on an SDV quality score of 0.78, so the library is run both as a generator and as the yardstick the comparison turns on.

title: Forensic-Oriented Intrusion Detection Using Synthetic Network Traffic Data and Explainable Artificial Intelligence

Everything the classifier sees is a synthetic derivative generated by SDV's CTGAN, which puts the library on the chain-of-custody boundary — remove it and the design has no training data it permits itself to use.

SDV is both the generator and the acceptance gate — what the paper calls the tool's built-in homogeneity score reports 89.3% concordance, and that number is what licenses the synthetic training set.

title: Synthesizing Tabular Microdata with Gaussian Copulas: The rsdv R Package
summary: Argues that R has had good pieces of the synthesis workflow but no native version of the copula-based joint model that SDV popularised, and introduces `rsdv` to close that gap: a Gaussian copula fitted jointly over numerical, categorical and boolean columns, with conditional sampling, declarative row-level constraints, and three reports. Benchmarked against synthpop and arf on UCI Adult, synthpop wins on marginal fidelity while rsdv matches it on privacy. This is a port of SDV's design into another language rather than a use of it — the metadata system, the constraint-by-rejection-sampling mechanism and the quality/validity/privacy reports are modelled directly on SDV and SDMetrics, and the package calls itself "the R Synthetic Data Vault".

title: A Comparative Study of Open-Source Libraries for Synthetic Tabular Data Generation: SDV vs. SynthCity

Synthcity's Bayesian Network takes fidelity; SDV's TVAE takes predictive utility at 1:10; neither library wins outright and the recommendation turns on documentation and ease of use, where SDV is judged the better tool for practitioners. SDV is run throughout, three synthesizers plus its statistical comparison functions, and it is half the subject matter rather than a baseline.
